svg.title: A wedge tracing with a giant v wave
svg.desc: An ECG above a wedge pressure tracing over three beats. Each beat shows a modest a wave near 16 mmHg at the end of the QRS and then a tall v wave peaking near 34 mmHg after the T wave, followed by a steep y descent. The v wave is more than 10 mmHg taller than the a wave. There is no dicrotic notch and the trace is rising, not falling, as the next QRS approaches, which is how it is told apart from a pulmonary artery trace of similar height.

g.text: Mean wedge here is near 18 mmHg and the a wave near 16, but the v wave dominates the mean. Haskell and
French found the mean overestimates LVEDP by about 30% in this situation.
Giant v waves are classically acute mitral regurgitation but are neither sensitive nor specific for it:
a stiff, small left atrium, a ventricular septal defect, or heart failure can produce them.
Report the a wave. Say which point you read, because the number changes with the choice.
